When Your Next PlayStation Game Is Just a Code: 100 Days After Sony Ended the Disc 💿

video // Oct 21, 2026

Watch on YouTube

Every one of us played a game we didn't buy. A big brother's hand-me-down. A copy a friend said you could bring back whenever. A disc that went around the whole neighborhood until it looked like it had been through a dishwasher.

None of that is possible with a download. 💿

On July 1, 2026, Sony announced that physical disc production for new PlayStation games ends in January 2028. My new documentary, 100 Days, follows everything that happened in the first hundred days after that announcement: who fought back, who folded, who got rich, and who's still standing in line with a plastic case in their hand.

What Sony actually announced

It started with a blog post. Four short paragraphs, no livestream, no trailer, no executive on a stage.

Starting January 2028, no new PlayStation game gets a disc. That's not just Sony's own games. It's every new game on PlayStation, from partner studios to third-party publishers.

Three things so nobody comes for me in the comments:

  • Your existing discs still work.
  • Games released on disc before the cutoff are unaffected.
  • Publishers can still order reprints of those older games after the deadline.

Sony's reason fits in one chart. From April to June, physical PlayStation games brought in about $128 million. Digital games and add-ons brought in about $3 billion. That's 24 to 1. From where Sony sits, the disc isn't a tradition. It's a rounding error.

And the timing? Days earlier, Rockstar confirmed the boxed version of Grand Theft Auto VI would have no disc inside. Just a download code in a box.

The internet fights back

The same day, the owner of a small Canadian game shop started a "Don't kill the disc" petition. It crossed 100,000 signatures in four days and has passed 386,000.

Then the brands showed up. Domino's UK went "digital pizza only," and KFC Spain said its chicken was now available as a PNG. When KFC is roasting you harder than the chicken, it's been a rough week.

Not everybody was laughing. Hideo Kojima said it made him very sad, and warned that once everything lives on somebody else's server, a company can switch it off. Even former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden said he didn't necessarily agree with the move.

Sony responds

On Sony's July 31 earnings call, the CFO said Sony had heard the strong views and would "cautiously move this forward." Forward, not backward. Sony told investors it wasn't seeing any impact on its business.

The future of the store shelf? A box with no disc, just a code inside. The cover art stays. The game becomes a one-time download code. And the trade-in, the resale, the second sale quietly disappears.

What happens to game stores?

For decades, stores barely made a dime selling you a new game. The real money came when that same disc came back through the door and got sold again.

Two independent shops refused to stock GTA VI because the box has no disc. GameStop's CEO said the diskless future "doesn't matter at all." His numbers show why: GameStop's sales fell, but collectibles jumped to 45% of the business, and it posted the highest second-quarter operating income in its history. GameStop didn't fight for the disc. GameStop left the building before the disc did.

Did the boycott work?

A preservation group called for a full PlayStation blackout from August 23 to 30: no logging in, no playing, no spending. When Circana's Mat Piscatella was asked whether it showed up in his US data, his answer was one word: no.

I wanted that one to work.

Xbox's Disc to Digital move

Then Xbox walked in at the worst possible moment for Sony. At Gamescom, Xbox announced Disc to Digital: put a supported Xbox One or Series X disc in your console and get a digital license for that game. It rolled out to everybody on September 29.

But the license is tied to the disc. Sell it or give it away, and that digital copy can be revoked. It's a bridge, not a gift. And Xbox still won't say whether its next console, Project Helix, has a disc drive.

The factory story, and the correction

In July, comments from Sony's distribution head got reported around the world as a 90% collapse at the last big factory pressing PlayStation discs, in Thalgau, Austria. In September, a Sony DADC spokesperson set the record straight: a decline by 10%, not down to 10%.

The disc isn't dying in one night. It's being phased out one new release at a time.

Players are still buying physical

Marvel's Wolverine became PlayStation's biggest UK physical launch of 2026. Santa Monica Studio told fans the next God of War will be available on disc. And over at Nintendo, about 38.5% of software sales were still physical in the April to June quarter.

Day 100: where things stand

  • The petition is still growing, but slower.
  • A UK class action covering about 12 million PlayStation Store customers is waiting on a verdict.
  • An antitrust complaint in Mexico is still with regulators.
  • GTA VI arrives November 19, and its boxed copy is the first real test of a game store without a disc.

Licensed, not sold

Here's the line that might outlive the whole fight. In a California lawsuit over the word "buy" on its store, Sony's own filing says the software is licensed to you, not sold.

Shawn Layden put it in plain English: if you can't sell a thing, do you own a thing?

Sony is probably going to win this one on paper. But starting January 2028, no new PlayStation game gets to become one of those hand-me-downs.

Selected sources (from the video): PlayStation Blog: disc production ending in January 2028, Sony quarterly financial data, GameStop second-quarter 2026 results, Rockstar: GTA VI pre-order support

Quick answers

When does Sony stop making PlayStation game discs? Physical disc production for new PlayStation games ends in January 2028. Games released on disc before then are unaffected, and older games can still be reprinted.

Will my PlayStation discs still work? Yes. Existing discs keep working. The cutoff only applies to new releases.

Does GTA VI come on a disc? No disc version has been announced. The boxed copy contains a download code.

What is Xbox Disc to Digital? An Xbox program that gives you a digital license for a supported disc you insert. The license stays tied to that disc, so selling or giving away the disc can revoke it.

Do you own your digital PlayStation games? Sony's own court filing says its software is licensed, not sold.

Your turn

What's one physical game you'll never sell? And when GTA VI drops as a code in a box, are you buying it anyway? 👇
